question: The disqualification of the membership of a State Legislature is laid down in which Article of the Indian Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is Article 191.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A person is** ineligible to be elected** to and to serve in **the Legislative Assembly or Legislative Council **of a State if they meet the following criteria: 

 
 
• If the** person occupies a paid position with the Government of India** or the Government of one of the States listed in the First Schedule, excluding a position that the State Legislature has decided by law is exempt from disqualification.
 
• If a court of competent jurisdiction has determined that **he is mentally ill**.
 
• If the **insolvent is yet unreleased**.
 
• If the **person is not an Indian citizen**, has chosen to become a citizen of another country, or has pledged their loyalty to another country.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 190**

 
 
• **Article 190(1)** states that **no one may serve** in **both houses of the legislature of a state** and that the legislature of the state shall provide by law for the vacation of any person elected to serve in both houses to travel home or to another location.
 
 
 
• **Article 144**
 
 
• The **Indian Constitution's Article 144 instructs civil and judicial agencies** to support** the Supreme Court in its work.** It states that the **Supreme Court** shall get assistance from all** civil and judicial bodies** within the boundaries of India. Additional Reading: Indian Supreme Court.
 
 
 
• **Article 14**
 
 
• Within the boundaries of India, the **State may not exclude anyone from enjoying equality** before the law or the equal protection of the laws because of their religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
